title: Counting Extrema of Cubics and Quartics
quickIdea: For a cubic, b^2 > 3ac gives one maximum and one minimum, b^2 = 3ac gives neither, b^2 < 3ac gives none at all. For a quartic, count the critical points where f' actually changes sign.
remember: For f(x) = ax^3 + bx^2 + cx + d with a != 0: f'(x) = 3ax^2 + 2bx + c, whose discriminant is 4(b^2 - 3ac).
b^2 > 3ac: two distinct stationary points, one local maximum and one local minimum.
b^2 = 3ac: exactly one stationary point, and it is an inflection, so no extremum.
b^2 < 3ac: f' has no real zero and f is strictly monotone, so no extremum.
For a quartic, f' is cubic, so there are at most three stationary points and at most two extrema; a repeated root of f' removes a candidate.

example.prompt: GATE CSE 2023 Q.18 by the cubic criterion: does f(x) = x^3 + 15x^2 - 33x - 36 have extrema, without solving f' = 0?
example.work: Here a = 1, b = 15, c = -33, so b^2 - 3ac = 225 - 3(1)(-33) = 225 + 99 = 324 > 0. Two distinct stationary points therefore exist, and since f'' = 6x + 30 has one zero, they lie on opposite sides of it and have opposite signs.
example.answer: One local maximum and one local minimum exist. Solving f' = 0 gives them explicitly at x = -11 (maximum) and x = 1 (minimum), confirming the criterion.

gateAngle: 2023 Q.18 offers the criterion as a shortcut (its accepted solutions show both the direct route and the b^2 - 3ac route) and 2008 Q.25 is the quartic counterpart where the count is decided by sign change. Together they are the two shapes GATE reuses for this topic.

variations.label: VERIFIED PYQ
variations.question: GATE CSE 2008 Q.25: the number of distinct extrema of 3x^4 - 16x^3 + 24x^2 + 37.
variations.why: f'(x) = 12x(x - 2)^2 has two zeros but the sign changes only at 0, so only one extremum exists.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: For which values of k does f(x) = x^3 + kx have a local maximum and a local minimum?
variations.answer: Exactly when k < 0. Here a = 1, b = 0, c = k, so b^2 - 3ac = -3k, which is positive only for k < 0.
variations.why: Turns the criterion into a condition on a parameter, which is how GATE has tested other calculus facts (for example the parameterised system-of-equations questions).

trap.what: Counting the solutions of f'(x) = 0 as the number of extrema.
trap.why: A repeated root of f' is a stationary point with no sign change, so it contributes nothing to the count.
trap.counterexample: 3x^4 - 16x^3 + 24x^2 + 37 has f'(x) = 12x(x - 2)^2 with the two zeros 0 and 2, but only one extremum, at 0.

check.question: How many extrema does f(x) = x^3 + 3x^2 + 3x + 1 have?
check.explanation: f(x) = (x + 1)^3, so f'(x) = 3(x + 1)^2 has the single double root -1 with no sign change. The criterion agrees: b^2 - 3ac = 9 - 9 = 0.
